findings.text: _covered_directory_shape caps its depth-first walk at 64 directories (:163) and expands children in sorted order, so a tree with wide subtrees never reaches the directory the plans live in. Measured against the repository's own tree with the landed function: `_covered_directory_shape(Path('/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/docs'))` returns 64 entries whose first six are ./.reckon/locks, ./.reckon/snapshots, ./.reckon/transactions, ./.reckon, ./_shared, ./archive, and './plans' is absent. The commit's stated purpose (a document added outside reckon and git must move the key) therefore does not hold on the production docs tree: a plan file added to docs/plans under docs/figures' 104 subdirectories still moves nothing and is answered from the snapshot until the 120 s revalidation window expires. The node's own fixture hides this because it builds one plans directory plus ten area directories, twelve readings against the cap of 64.

The plan's key bound is `at most 8 os.stat or open calls per mounted project for its key, counted with a wrapper over both`. The gained diff threads a `dirs` counter through the driver (:67, :82-87) and returns early for every directory stat before the `covered` and `keys` counters are touched, so the directory stats the new shape walk makes are counted nowhere and asserted nowhere; `counts["dirs"]` is incremented and never read. `assert measured["key_calls_per_project"] <= 8` at :599 therefore passes for any number of directory stats the key takes, including the 64-per-mount-per-key-build the shape walk performs on a wide tree. The exclusion was directed by the coordinator's instruction to add one stat per directory, so the plan's bound and the directed change conflict; the conflict is resolved here by not measuring it.

`from reckon.metadata_index import _dir_identity` reaches under the public owner of exactly this capability. reckon/metadata_index.py:168 `covered_dir_identity(path)` is the documented entry point and it reuses the observation inside an open discovery pass (`_DISCOVERY_DIRS`), while `_dir_identity` (:879) re-stats every call. The read path runs the key twice (before and after the recompute in reckon/mcp.py:1837 and :1860), so every covered directory is stat'd twice per read where the owner would have made the second observation free.

`roadmap_snapshot_path` now files one file per resolved docs root, `roadmap-snapshot-<digest>.json`, in the shared node-local cache directory, and nothing removes a file whose tree is gone. Before this change one file served a project name; now every temporary tree a test, scratch checkout or short-lived worktree composes in leaves a snapshot behind in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/reckon/<project>/ for the life of the node's cache. Bounded per file, unbounded in count over a long-lived node.

No case in the node's own test file distinguishes two trees or two crew homes that declare one project name. `_snapshot_files` (:587) globs a single fixture root, so replacing `roadmap_docs_identity` or `crew_home_identity` with a constant would leave every assertion in this file green: the in-process memo key at :432-434 and :467-469, the file name and the two key fields are all unexercised by an independent value. The regressions these digests prevent are caught only incidentally by other test files in the population under -n 8 (tests/test_every_resume_door_states_its_deadline.py, tests/test_ready_sections_are_ranked.py), which is real but is not a guard the node added.

The ruff arm named four paths (reckon/serve.py, reckon/mcp.py, reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py, tests/test_a_roadmap_read_answers_from_its_snapshot.py) and reached 27 findings against 27 at base. The second gained commit, 280bf2cf5, also edits tests/test_every_surface_lists_open_decisions.py, which no lint arm covered, so the manifest's claim of no added findings does not extend to one of the two test files the increment changed.
